data.narrative:
**1872 Valuation Narrative**

1872 is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $15M to date, founded by Dan Summers. The valuation analysis draws from a universe of 9 private robotics and manufacturing peers (including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI) and 1 public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ), though the peer set remains constrained at the seed stage within this sector.

The stage-progression method is applicable and forms the sole quantitative anchor for this analysis. Using total capital raised as a valuation proxy of $15M, a typical seed-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.5x implies a post-money valuation of $38M. This method applies standard industry progression assumptions without company-specific revenue or growth data. A peer-median approach was considered but rejected due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables in the narrow robotics manufacturing cohort—only 1 same-stage peer was identified, falling below the minimum threshold of 3 for reliable triangulation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $32M to $43M, centered on a median of $38M. This reflects approximately 2.1x to 2.9x the raised capital. Primary uncertainties include the thinness of seed-stage peer data in this sector, reliance on stage progression absent company-specific metrics, and lack of revenue or burn-rate visibility. Validation would benefit from founder-provided financial projections or closer comparables at similar deployment stages.
